title: AI-REACT - ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE READINESS EVALUATION AND ASSESSMENT FOR EARTH SCIENCE CHALLENGES AND OPPORTUNITIES - EXPRO PLUS
description: Strategic assessment activity to evaluate the readiness of artificial intelligence to support Earth system science and future ESA Earth Observation missions. The activity will assess AI approaches across the EO Science Strategy and its Overarching Science Themes,with a focus on identifying where AI is already delivering credible scientific value, where important scientific and technical gapsremain, and where maturity is sufficient to support mission-facing tasks such as geophysical observables retrieval development, observation requirement definition, observing-system analysis, and science-gap identification. It will build a structured evidence base, assess scientific rigour and mission relevance, and develop an AI readiness framework aligned with ESA readiness principles, leadingto a roadmap for FutureEO investments and follow-on actions. A core outcome of the study is a decision-ready assessment of where AIcan credibly strengthen future EO mission science and planning, and where further evidence or development is still required.

title: NAVISP-EL1-131-CHIP SCALE OPTICAL ATOMIC CLOCK FOR PNT APPLICATIONS EXPRO+ REISSUE OF (1-13610)
description: Development of a compact optical atomic clock module (physics package) for PNT applications. The activity will design, manufacture,and test an Engineering Model (EM) of a chip-scale optical clock exploiting an atomic optical transition to achieve 10 improved stability (target timing drift 10-30 ns/day) versus existing microwave clocks. The clock will provide a stabilized optical frequencyoutput in a low-power (< 5 W), compact device. Tasks include detailed thermo-mechanical design for robust operation in harsh environments, definition of low-power control electronics requirements and autonomous operation algorithms, assembly of the optical clock physics package, and development of Electrical Ground Support Equipment (EGSE) to control and test the EM. The EM will undergo performance verification in ambient and thermal conditions to demonstrate its stability, targeting TRL 4-5 and paving the way for future space-qualified ultra-stable timing solutions for navigation and timing systems.

title: COMPATIBILITY VALIDATION TESTBED OF THE OPTICAL HEAD AND ITS CONTROL OF OPTICAL COMMUNICATION TERMINALS (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 5H.015)
description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to develop a testbed that will test the interoperability between different suppliers of optical communication terminals. Thisshall include free-space optics testing to evaluate the pointing, acquisition, and tracking performance.TargetedImprovements:To enable independent on-ground validation of optical communication terminal interoperability ina facility located in ESA member states.Description: With an increasing number of constellations considering the use of optical inter satellite links and cross-atmospheric links, it is important to test, validateand ultimately certify the interoperability between different laser terminals manufactured by multiple suppliers.This activity will develop the capability of enabling independent interoperability validation between various laser communication terminals. The focus willbe on pointing, acquisition and tracking performance validation for both intersatellite and cross-atmospheric optical links. The developed testbed shallenable the performancevalidation of the terminal optical head in free space, and the compatibility validation of the pointing, acquisition and trackingsequence implemented by optical terminal (both space and ground) suppliers. The testbed will enable the validation to be carried out between two terminalsunder test from different suppliers and shall be accessible to all the ESA member states industries.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). title: MATURATION OF ZERO BOIL OFF COMPONENTS (RTB CRYOCOOLER) OF LIQUID OXYGEN (LOX) - EXPRO+
description: Objective:  To design and develop a cryocooler breadboard model, based on the Reverse Turbo-Brayton, targeting LOx temperature, for the long duration storage of liquid cryogenic propellants for in Space application. Description:  Cryogenic propellants are being considered and baselined for future missions as a valid alternative to storable propellants for orbital and deep space missions.A combination of Liquid Oxygen (LOX) and Liquid cryogenic propellants provide significant advantages in term of performance over storable fuel and oxidizers.  Several classes of orbital and deep space missions can benefit from cryogenic propulsion systems. However, cryogenic propulsion systems technologies are only available for short duration missions (max. 1 day, launchers). Extending the operating life of these systems requires a range of new technologies, more adapted to high volume transfer at lower pressure, andfor a long-time duration of operations and long cycles in space (days to weeks).  Handling cryogenic fluid in space for long duration necessitates the introduction of a so called Zero Boil off systems where active cooling systems are needed.  In order to increase TRL for such system and especially for the cryocooler part, this activity targets to design, manufacture a testing model and perform test under representative environment on ground, targeting the LOx temperature range, of around 90K, coinciding also with sub-cooled LCH4, and would also demonstrate the first technological bricks for a LH2 RTB cryocooler of such size. Also the heat lifts is targeted to be in the range of 100-200W, which is considered an important stepping stone into enabling zero boil-off components storage in-orbit of cryogenic propellants.   This activity encompasses the following tasks:   - - - - Requirements definition, design trade-offs, a development plan, industrial plan (incl. make or buy analyses) to reach TRL4 at the end of the activity at component level, A systems sizing exercise (considering ZBO LOX tank application), and the associated detailed design of the 90K Class RTB Breadboard Test plan, HW manufacturing and testing Test results exploitation, lessons learned and recommendations for future or complementary development Deliverables: Breadboard, Report
